clue.text: Passing comments about faulty lines I put in

indicators.note: says the letter I is placed inside the jumbled letters
something faulty is out of order, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

parts.note: RY, short for railway, is a crossword staple for lines

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about bad lines of verse they have added to a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' means death here, not going by; 'faulty' makes OBTUA and 'put in' takes I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's notice of a death is commentary on someone's passing.

clue.text: African port, say, raised fruit

parts.note: Oran is a port city in Algeria

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters read upwards, back to front

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: An African port has, for example, grown its fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: This citrus is one of the best-known fruits.

clue.text: One can spout about European traveller

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the words for can and spout go around the European letter

parts.note: a tin is a can
to spout is to rant

explanation.surface: A European traveller who can hold forth at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who journeys from place to place, such as a wandering worker, is a traveller.

clue.text: College about to form alliance

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A college is about to join a partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: A federation or partnership of groups joined together is an alliance.

clue.text: Iris drops Bob

parts.note: raindrops falling are rain
to bob is to bow or curtsy briefly

explanation.surface: A woman called Iris dumps her boyfriend Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iris' and 'Bob' look like names; Iris is the Greek goddess of the rainbow, and her name means it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Iris personified the arc of colours in the sky, so the name stands for it.

clue.text: Unnamed wild flower

indicators.note: having no name means losing N, the standard abbreviation for name

parts.note: a wild, raging person is violent

explanation.surface: A wild flower nobody has bothered to name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unnamed' looks like an adjective on the flower, but it removes N (name) from VIOLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small purple or blue spring bloom is a common example of a flower.

clue.text: Popular goalie entertains northern host

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so the letter sits inside

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a goalie is a goalkeeper, or keeper

explanation.surface: A well-liked goalkeeper plays host to someone from the North.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlord of a pub or inn is the host who looks after guests.

clue.text: River left mineral deposit skirting island

indicators.note: the deposit runs around the edge of the island, enclosing it

parts.note: ore is a natural deposit of mineral

explanation.surface: A river has left a mineral deposit round the edge of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: France's longest waterway flows through its chateau country to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Coin made from copper core

wordplay.reading: PP, the core of COPPER, read as two P

parts.note: the core of the word copper is its middle pair of letters, PP, which reads as two of the coin abbreviated p

explanation.surface: A coin is minted from a core of copper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like the metal, but its middle letters PP read as 2p.
explanation.definitionFit: The old British piece worth two pennies was a coin, as is the modern 2p.

clue.text: I obtain wound around eye, say, from scratch

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit around the single letter
wound, as in twisted around, signals the letters of these words being rearranged
say means the word eye is spoken, giving the sound of a letter

parts.note: eye is pronounced like the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone gets a bandage wrapped around an injured eye and has to start again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' rearranges I OBTAIN; 'around' puts that round I, the sound of 'eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means from the beginning, the same idea as starting over completely.

clue.text: Pea plant's doing badly, I gathered

indicators.note: the jumbled letters gather up the I, taking it inside
doing something badly suggests it is done wrongly, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A gardener reports that the pea plant is struggling, or so they have heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' jumbles DOING; 'gathered' takes I inside it. The plant gives a blue dye and belongs to the pea family.
explanation.definitionFit: The dye-producing shrub of this name is a legume, a member of the pea family.

clue.text: Squander ball user in odd positions

indicators.note: take the letters in the first, third, fifth and seventh places of the words

explanation.surface: Someone who uses a ball wastes it by playing out of position.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to blow money recklessly is to waste it, the sense here.

clue.text: Ecofriendly engineers accessing data

indicators.note: accessing suggests getting into something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: gen is British slang for information or data
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a regiment of the British Army

explanation.surface: Environmentally minded engineers are getting at the figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Environmentally sound policies and products are routinely described by this colour.

clue.text: Bred nearly 11 bananas in gazebo

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so the letters are scrambled
nearly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the number written out as a word

explanation.surface: Someone raised eleven banana plants inside a garden summerhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts ELEVEN to ELEVE; 'bananas' scrambles BRED plus ELEVE. The 11 here is the number, not 11-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A summerhouse or raised turret built to give a fine view is a form of garden pavilion.

clue.text: The way to keep fresh yam crop piled up in barn

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: how means the way or manner

indicators.note: fresh signals new, so the letters are made anew in another order

explanation.surface: Advice on keeping a yam harvest fresh by storing it in a barn.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a long phrase for stored hay; 'fresh' makes AYM, which 'to keep' holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried grass stacked in a barn, or the loft where it is stored, goes by this term.

clue.text: Staff work out course for cutter

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it
to do a sum is to work it out
a line is a course or route taken

explanation.surface: Employees plan a route for a vessel or a gemstone cutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' is a verb here, to man.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen slicer with an adjustable blade for vegetables is a type of cutter.

clue.text: Houseman, one in Morecambe, relying on experience

indicators.note: the pieces are placed in the comedian's first name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, half of Morecambe and Wise
a member of the House of Commons is an MP
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A junior hospital doctor, one of them working in the seaside town of Morecambe, learns on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Houseman' suggests a junior doctor, but it is an MP. 'Morecambe' is the comedian Eric, not the Lancashire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Empirical knowledge comes from observation and practice rather than theory; this adjective is the older form.

clue.text: Wedding party check in here

definitions.meaning: the formal party held after a marriage ceremony
the front desk of a hotel where guests sign in

explanation.surface: Wedding guests are told to sign in at this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a formal post-wedding party and a hotel's front desk.

clue.text: Small pick lacking length and range

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a plectrum is a guitar pick

explanation.surface: A small guitar pick that lacks length and reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A full spread of views or colours is a range.

clue.text: Plant barrel, one hidden by vegetable

indicators.note: the pieces are covered by the vegetable, set inside its letters

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
a tun is a large cask or barrel
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gardener plants up a barrel, one that is screened by vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: This trumpet-flowered bedding annual is a popular garden plant.

clue.text: Bread supplier stocks nothing, or almost nothing

indicators.note: the machine stocks the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: bread is slang for money, and a cash machine (ATM) supplies it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A baker carries no stock, or next to none.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread supplier' suggests a baker; bread is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle so tiny it is a byword for the smallest amount, as in not an iota.

clue.text: Hijacking plot to free prisoners

indicators.note: freeing the prisoners means taking them out of the word for plot

parts.note: a plot is a conspiracy
cons, short for convicts, are prisoners

explanation.surface: A plane is seized as part of a scheme to release jailed comrades.
explanation.definitionFit: Seizing a ship or aircraft by force is the sea-robbery crime extended to the air.

clue.text: Top rock group blocks promenade

indicators.note: the band blocks the promenade, standing inside it

parts.note: a pier is a seaside promenade
REM is an American rock band

explanation.surface: The best rock band is obstructing the seafront walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: Foremost or leading, as in a first-class league, means top.

clue.text: What papers eventually do for chicken

definitions.meaning: a chicken is a coward, lacking courage

explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' looks like the bird, but it means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageing paper turns this colour, and the same word means cowardly.

clue.text: Senior officer on board or in relief unit

indicators.note: the word or is placed in the piece of furniture

parts.note: a commode is a chair housing a chamber pot, where one relieves oneself

explanation.surface: An officer is either aboard ship or in a unit sent to relieve others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief unit' suggests troops sent as reinforcements, but it is a commode.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval rank above captain, or the senior captain of a convoy, commands at sea.

clue.text: Miniature painter Joan tours clubs

indicators.note: the painter goes round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: Joan Miró was a Spanish surrealist painter
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: A miniature painter called Joan goes round the clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefix-word meaning very small, as in a tiny car or computer.

clue.text: Fruit drink 8 swallowed

indicators.note: the drink swallows the letters, taking them inside

parts.note: ale is a drink
8-down is a coin worth two pennies, written 2p, so two Ps

explanation.surface: A fruit drink knocked back by a small coin's worth of change.
explanation.walkthrough: The 8 points to 8-down, a coin written 2p: that gives the letters PP.
explanation.definitionFit: This orchard produce is one of the commonest fruits.

clue.text: American sailors grip firm piece of mast

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
RN is the Royal Navy, the British fleet

explanation.surface: American sailors hold a sturdy section of a ship's mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mast' looks like a ship's spar, but it is the nuts of forest trees fallen to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Mast is the fallen fruit of oak and beech trees, and an oak nut is one piece of it.

clue.text: Sports ground approaches crude shrink

indicators.note: one piece comes up to the other, so they are placed side by side

parts.note: rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public sports field
crude is unrefined oil

explanation.surface: A sports ground is next to a crude shrink, perhaps a tactless psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrink' looks like a psychiatrist noun, but it is the verb meaning to draw back.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch or draw back in fear or disgust is to recoil.

clue.text: Discard old mail originally bearing two names

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away

indicators.note: originally suggests the letters arranged as they first were, before any order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Throw away old post that was originally addressed to two people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Linnaean scientific naming system gives each species a genus name and a species name, two in all.

clue.text: Tied up low tomato, for instance

parts.note: to low is to make the sound of cattle
a ripe tomato is an example of something coloured red

explanation.surface: A short tomato plant is tied up to a cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective describing the tomato, but it is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat secured with ropes at a quay is fastened in place.

clue.text: Mint concoction with last of gin thrown in

indicators.note: the pieces are tossed inside the concoction

parts.note: a brew is a mixture or concoction
and means together with

indicators.note: says to take only the final letter of the word gin

explanation.surface: A mint-flavoured mixed drink with the dregs of the gin thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' looks like the herb in a cocktail, but it means in perfect new condition.
explanation.definitionFit: In mint condition means unused, fresh from the maker.
